findings.title: Unsubscribe crashes when TopicUser is nil
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe does TopicUser.find_by(user_id: current_user.id, topic_id: params[:topic_id]) and then immediately dereferences tu.notification_level. find_by returns nil when the user has no TopicUser row for the topic (never visited/interacted). This raises NoMethodError on nil and returns 500 instead of unsubscribing. The consequence is users clicking the email link for a topic they never visited get an error page and the notification level is never changed.

findings.title: State-changing GET enables CSRF / prefetch unsubscribes
findings.body: TopicsController#unsubscribe mutates notification_level (regular->muted or watching/tracking->regular) inside a GET action with skip_before_filter :check_xhr. GETs are not CSRF-protected in Rails, are pre-fetched by email clients/browsers, and can be triggered cross-site via img/link. An attacker or a mail scanner can silently mute or downgrade a victim's topic subscription without consent. Mutating actions must be POST/PUT with CSRF protection and ideally a confirmation/token, not GET.

findings.title: New unsubscribe_link interpolation breaks emails without unsubscribe_url
findings.body: config/locales/server.en.yml now defines unsubscribe_link with two interpolations: %{user_preferences_url} and %{unsubscribe_url}. Email::MessageBuilder#body and #html_part call I18n.t('unsubscribe_link', template_args) for every email with add_unsubscribe_link true. Only notification emails now supply unsubscribe_url; any other current or future caller with add_unsubscribe_link true but no unsubscribe_url will raise I18n::MissingInterpolationArgument (or render broken text), failing email delivery. The template change makes a previously optional argument required.

findings.title: Unescaped topic title rendering enables XSS
findings.body: The unsubscribe template uses triple-mustache {{{stopNotificiationsText}}} where stopNotificiationsText interpolates model.fancyTitle into an I18n string. Triple-mustache disables HTML escaping, so any HTML/JS in the topic title is injected into the page. Topic titles are user-controlled; even with server-side escaping, client-side fancyTitle handling plus unescaped insertion creates a stored-XSS vector for anyone visiting the unsubscribe URL.

findings.title: afterModel assumes topic.details always exists
findings.body: topic-unsubscribe route does topic.set("details.notificationReasonText", null) without checking that details is present. If PostStream.loadTopicView returns JSON without details (permissions, deleted topic, API change, or error payload), the nested set fails or throws, breaking the unsubscribe page transition. The code needs a guard for missing details and rejection handling for the loadTopicView promise.
